claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni EHEA has a coarse, straight dual-phase fcc/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial alloy exhibits interfacial cracking and low room-temperature ductility.
Elevated-temperature severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing can convert straight lamellae into a fine, wavy or patterned configuration.
A deformation window of 600–800 °C, total strain above 4, strain rate of 10^-3 to 10^-2 s^-1, and pressure above 5 GPa for HPT will produce the proposed patterned structure.
Annealing at 500–600 °C for 10–30 minutes will relieve residual stress without coarsening the lamellae.
The treatment will reduce the lamellar spacing below 500 nm and increase interface curvature and boundary dislocation density.
A patterned fcc/B2 interface configuration will distribute stress concentrations more evenly and prevent localized crack initiation.
A higher density of fine lamellar interfaces provides additional dislocation sources and sinks.
Curved interfaces interrupt straight, continuous crack paths along fcc/B2 boundaries.
Dislocations will shear or bypass the B2 phase more uniformly, producing high strain hardening and uniform plasticity.
High pressure during deformation suppresses void nucleation and promotes interface bonding.
Short annealing stabilizes the patterned structure against coarsening.
The treated alloy will attain an ultimate tensile strength above 1.2 GPa.
The treated alloy will retain elongation to fracture above 25%.
The fracture mode will change from interfacial cracking to ductile dimple rupture.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has an fcc/B2 lamellar microstructure with approximately 2 μm inter-lamellar spacing.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a room-temperature tensile strength of approximately 944 MPa and elongation of approximately 25.6%.
Excessively high pressure may induce a brittle HCP transformation analogous to that observed in a Ta-containing refractory HEA.
HIP at 1200 °C and 150 MPa for four hours approximates the conventional HIP conditions reported in PMC5578249.
Failure of HIP alone to form a wavy structure or improve ductility would falsify the claim that the patterned high-intensity thermomechanical treatment is required.

contradictions.description: The initial state is characterized as having low ductility, but the stated as-cast baseline elongation is already 25.6%, and the target of greater than 25% is described as an improvement or maintenance of ductility.

The rule says that failure of HIP alone would falsify the need for the proposed patterned treatment, but immediately says the same result would confirm that HIP alone is insufficient and that the specialized treatment is required. The result is corroborative, not falsifying.
